harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up rootless Podman on node1 (Alpine/OpenRC) running as unprivileged user appsvc, serving nginx on port 8080, auto-starting at boot via the podman-openrc service with restart=always, with no PAM login session ever created for appsvc.
actions_performed: Installed podman, shadow-uidmap, slirp4netns, fuse-overlayfs on node1
Created unprivileged user appsvc (uid 1001) with home dir, no login session mechanism used
Configured /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid for appsvc rootless user namespaces
Enabled and started the cgroups OpenRC service at boot runlevel
Verified rootless podman works as appsvc via su + XDG_RUNTIME_DIR
Pulled nginx:alpine and ran it as appsvc with -p 8080:80 --restart=always --name webapp
Configured /etc/conf.d/podman with podman_user=appsvc and enabled podman service in default runlevel (uses start_containers to auto-start restart=always containers)
Discovered /run/user/1001 (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) is not created automatically on Alpine/OpenRC boot (no systemd/pam_systemd), causing podman service to fail at boot
Created custom OpenRC service /etc/init.d/appsvc-runtimedir to create and chown /run/user/1001 before podman starts, added to default runlevel with 'before podman' dependency

Verified end-to-end: rebooted node1 once to discover the runtime-dir gap, fixed it, then rebooted node1 a second time and confirmed the container came up fully automatically with no manual intervention
Confirmed via ps/last/who that no login session exists for appsvc while the container runs, and HTTP 200 is served from $NODE_IP:8080

evidence.requirement: Container app runs as unprivileged user appsvc, serving on port 8080
evidence.summary: podman run as appsvc with -p 8080:80; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns 200 and HTML content; ps shows nginx master owned by appsvc, workers under mapped uid 100100

podman-openrc service (podman_user=appsvc) enabled in default runlevel; discovered missing /run/user/1001 broke boot-time start, fixed with custom appsvc-runtimedir OpenRC service ordered before podman; after fix, second reboot shows both services auto-started and container running within 7 seconds of boot with no manual commands

evidence.requirement: No active login session for appsvc while service runs
evidence.summary: who/last show no TTY/login entries for appsvc while nginx and podman processes run under that uid; container is launched by root's supervise-daemon calling su, not an interactive/login session
Captured boot_id e561ef47..., podman/cgroups service status started, podman ps showing webapp Up, HTTP 200, and no login session, prior to first reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command returned immediately; subsequent polls hit connection reset/timeout confirming disconnection; boot_id changed from e561ef47... to 947efb1d... after first reboot, and from 947efb1d... to 935e96cf... after the second verification reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of services, data, and app
evidence.summary: After second reboot with the fix in place, appsvc-runtimedir and podman both show started in rc-status, podman ps shows the same webapp container (same ID, created earlier, now Up 7s) automatically restarted, curl to port 8080 returns 200 with real content, and no login session exists for appsvc
